name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and accurately reflects the behavior: scans the menu/template party roster and reports whether a char with the given char_id is present. No Ghidra address residue in the name. The _id suffix is semantic (it disambiguates char_id from job_id/class and corrects the documented old misnomer fd2_check_party_has_char_class).
purpose: Returns whether the menu/template party roster contains a character whose char_id (init value) equals the argument.
logic_summary: Linear scan over [0, data_fd2_shared_menu_party_member_count): for each 0x50-byte template entry in the buffer at data_fd2_shared_menu_party_roster_buffer_ptr, compares the byte at offset +0x08 (char_id_init) against char_id; returns 1 on the first match, 0 if the scan exhausts. __CHK(8) is the compiler-generated stack-probe prologue.

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: char_id to look for: the init char_id (the value passed to fd2_init_runtime_char_from_base_growth when the char joined), compared against each template entry's +0x08 byte. Callers pass concrete char_ids such as 0xC (凱麗) and 0x12 (蜜蒂). NOT a job_id/class.
params.reason: Live Ghidra parameter is the generic placeholder param_1, which does not describe its use as a char_id; rename to char_id (the name the src already uses). Recorded only; applied in Stage 2.

returns.semantics: 1 if a template-party entry with matching char_id is found, 0 otherwise.

notes: Source comment block (misc.c lines 109-134) is already precise, correct, ASCII-clean, and matches the live decompile (count global, 0x50 stride, +0x08 char_id byte, __CHK(8) prologue, 7 callers); kept as-is. Ghidra plate is more verbose but consistent with this understanding, so left untouched. Body is a simple correct linear scan; no logic issues.
